findings.text: follow-on: the guard `pointer_path(existing_run_id).exists()` then `read_pointer(existing_run_id)` is race-free only because every pointer remover takes the same per-run lock this read holds. I verified each unlink site: promotion.discard (reckon/crew/promotion.py:1259), the reap in reckon/crew/routing.py:1757, and complete/withdraw (reckon/crew/promotion.py:1188 and reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:189, both reached under `with _pointer_lock(run_id)` at promotion.py:183). No test asserts that invariant, so a future pointer remover that unlinks without the per-run lock would silently reopen the window the guard closes. Not blocking — the fix is correct against every remover present at this head.

justifications.durability: the guard is load-bearing and falsified: restoring the raising read makes the new case fail with CrewError "no live run 'r-racing'" (EXIT=1, the run's negative-control.log, which I read and independently reproduced against base code). The new case reddens on a future re-introduction of the unconditional re-read. Below 20 because the guard's correctness rests on an invariant — every pointer remover holds the per-run lock — that no test asserts; I verified all four current unlink sites hold it, but a lock-free remover added later would reopen the window silently.

justifications.fit: the change sits inside queue_dispatch where the re-queue already lived, in the same style as the surrounding pointer handling; the comment explains the mechanism (a pointer discarded under the re-queue is treated as absent) rather than a ticket; no plan, sprint or ticket identifier appears in any symbol, path or comment. The `requeued` flag is a small, clear control-flow addition.
justifications.goal_fidelity: section 6's deliverable is met in full and independently verified: a pointer that vanished between the scan and the lock is treated as absent, one fresh queued pointer is written under the request's own run id, no error is raised, and tests/test_held_dispatch_is_queued.py passes (12 passed at head).
